title: supply-demand-cost-scaler-and-presets-generator
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Introduce supply-demand cost scaler that generates conservative batching/cache/quant presets and a shadow-run prober for safe rollout. Adds CLI tooling to simulate unit-econ scenarios. No public API changes.
description:
Motivation: Customers need safe, automated defaults for batching, cache warmup, and quant profiles that reflect real traffic patterns without risking regressions. This PR implements a supply-demand based cost scaler that synthesizes conservative presets from live or synthetic traffic, plus a "shadow-run" collector that can run alongside existing routes to gather signals for profile generation. The goal is to provide high-quality starter profiles for Redwood Optimize that reduce unit cost while preserving latency SLOs and sample quality.

What this change includes:
- New service: econ.scaler.Service - takes traffic histograms and capacity/latency targets and outputs candidate presets (batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, kv_cache_ttl, quant_profile).
- Shadow-run collector: lightweight in-proc tracer that logs per-request latency/seq-length/kv-hit metrics when enabled for a route. Config is off by default and gated behind canary flags.
- Presets generator CLI: rwd-econ generate-presets --input ./shadow.json --output presets.yaml to create YAML presets that can be applied via Console or Dedicated configs.
- Simulation harness: a small Monte Carlo workload prober (economics/sim) used in tests to validate that suggested presets meet cost & latency constraints under synthetic scenarios.
- Metrics & dashboards: adds econ.* Prometheus metrics and a Grafana dashboard JSON to observability-pack.

Commits (high-level):
- feat(econ): add supply-demand scaler core algorithm (2 commits)
- feat(cli): presets generator and simple YAML serializer (1 commit)
- feat(shadow): add collector middleware and sampling knobs (3 commits)
- test(econ): add simulation harness and unit tests (2 commits)
- docs: usage guide + Console integration notes (1 commit)

Files/areas changed (high level):
- src/economics/scaler.go (new)
- cmd/rwd-econ/main.go (new)
- pkg/shadow/collector.go (new), pkg/shadow/middleware.go (updated)
- observability/dashboards/econ-presets.json (new)
- internal/sim/montecarlo_test.go (new)
- docs/optimizers/presets.md (new)
- Makefile + CI: added econ unit and integration job shims

Small illustrative snippet (presets YAML example):
  # presets.yaml (generated)
  route: /v1/generate
  preset_name: conservative-small
  batch_size: 8
  max_batch_latency_ms: 40
  kv_cache_ttl_ms: 30000
  quant_profile: q4_0_opt

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests for scaler heuristics and end-to-end smoke for CLI.
- Integration job 'econ-integration' was flaky on first run (timing-dependent); retried once and all checks passed.
- CI matrix covers go1.20 and go1.22 builds. Final CI status: pass.

Review conversation (summary):
- Diego Martinez (review): "Nice isolation of the scaler logic. Two notes: 1) ensure metadata about canary sampling rate is surfaced in Console; 2) consider making the quant_profile suggestion conservative (prefer higher-precision by default)."
- Ava Chen (author): "Addressed both: added console flag docs and bumped default to q4_0_opt; added unit tests to assert no more than 5% quality drop in simulation for suggested profiles."
- Priya Srinivasan (review): "Can we add an opt-out annotation for Dedicated customers that don't want shadow telemetry?"
- Ava Chen: "Added annotation 'redwood.econ/disable-shadow' and a dedicated-only guard. Documented in presets.md."
- Liam O'Neill (approval): "Local runs look good; simulation harness makes regressions visible. Approving."

Safety and rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind 'econ-shadow' feature flag. Shadow-run off by default.
- Presets are generated as suggestions only; application requires explicit apply via Console or CLI to change runtime settings.
- Added an "inspect-only" mode for the CLI to evaluate presets without writing to disk.

Backward compatibility: No runtime-breaking changes. All defaults remain unchanged until a preset is explicitly applied.

Performance notes: In internal load tests, presets generated by the scaler reduced per-token CPU time by ~12% on median workloads while keeping p99 latency within configured SLOs. Results vary by model and sequence-length distribution.

Related work: ENG-7123 (project to standardize unit-econ signals), ENG-7190 (presets UI flow).

Merge: Squash-merged by Diego Martinez after green CI and approvals.

Follow-ups planned:
- Telemetry sampler dashboard (ENG-7235)
- Auto-suggest opt-in emails for customers who've run the shadow collector for >72h
- More conservative quantization verifier that runs sample prompts through a golden-eval set before applying a preset
